newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Hyundai plans $200 mln plant in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai plans $200 mln plant in Malaysia.

text.p: Hyundai Electronics Industries Co Ltd, a unit of South Korea's Hyundai Group, said it was planning to invest $200 million in a plant in northern Malaysia, local newspapers said on Saturday.
The plant, located in Kulim High Tech park in northern Kedah state, will make parts for the hard disc drives of one of its U.S. units, Maxtor Corp.
The newspapers quoted Hyundai Electronics president Y.H. Kim as saying that the plant was being set up in joint venture with Hyundai Electronics America, the group's North American unit.
The 18,600 square-metre plant would employ about 1,500 people, Kim said, adding that the first phase of the project would cost $200 million.
"Production is expected to commence in the first quarter of 1999 and the facility is projected to generate an annual revenue of about 600 million ringgit," Kim said.
